findings.suggestion: Make the configured value load-bearing or delete it. Cheapest consistent option: have `LinkPolicyConfig.urlValidator(...)` pass `properties.links().maxUrlLength()` into `UrlValidator` (it already passes `baseUrl`), and drop the now-redundant hardcoded constant; keep `@Size(max = 2048)` only if you reference a shared constant, since a bean-validation annotation needs a compile-time constant.
findings.summary: The maximum long-URL length exists three times and only two of them agree by accident: `UrlValidator.MAX_URL_LENGTH = 2048`, `@Size(max = 2048)` on `CreateLinkRequest.longUrl` (line 25), and `app.links.max-url-length: 2048` in application.yml bound to `AppProperties.Links.maxUrlLength` — which no code reads. Raising the limit in config changes nothing, and a reviewer would reasonably believe it did.

findings.suggestion: Write `@Pattern(regexp = AliasPolicy.PATTERN)` — it is a `public static final String`, so it is a valid annotation constant — and delete the comment. If a package cycle is unwanted, move `PATTERN` to the `api` package and have `AliasPolicy` reference it.
findings.summary: The alias charset rule is a literal regex on the DTO and again as `AliasPolicy.PATTERN`. `AliasPolicy` even carries the comment "identical to the one on the request DTO", which documents the drift risk rather than removing it — and `PATTERN` also duplicates `MIN_LENGTH`/`MAX_LENGTH` inside its own literal.

findings.suggestion: Drop the inline default — `@Scheduled(fixedDelayString = "${app.click.flush-interval}")` — since `@DefaultValue("PT5S")` plus application.yml already supply it, and add a one-line comment on `AppProperties.Click.flushInterval` saying it is consumed by the annotation rather than by a constructor, so the accessor does not read as dead.
findings.summary: `@Scheduled(fixedDelayString = "${app.click.flush-interval:PT5S}")` reaches past the typed configuration surface that the rest of the change uses uniformly (`AppProperties`), and restates the PT5S default that `AppProperties.Click.flushInterval` already declares. `AppProperties.Click.flushInterval()` is consequently read by nothing, so the documented accessor and the actual schedule can diverge silently.

findings.suggestion: Delete the unused `LinkEntity.isResolvableAt` and have `CachedLink.redirectsAt` be the single statement of the rule, or express both in terms of one static predicate on `LinkStatus`. Whichever way, one of the two should stop existing.
findings.summary: "A link redirects when it is ACTIVE and not yet expired" is expressed twice: `CachedLink.redirectsAt` and `LinkEntity.statusAt`/`isResolvableAt`. They must agree — adding a fourth `LinkStatus` or changing the expiry boundary from exclusive to inclusive has to be done in both — and `LinkEntity.isResolvableAt` is currently called by nothing, so nothing would fail if only one copy were updated.

findings.suggestion: Move the container-independent helpers to static methods on `ApiClient` or `Fixtures` (e.g. `Fixtures.givenLink(api, bearer)`, `ApiClient.clickRepeatedly(api, code, times)`) and have both base classes delegate, so the restart harness inherits nothing but still shares one definition of each helper.
findings.summary: `alice()`, `bob()`, `givenLink(bearer)`, `sleep(Duration)` and `clickRepeatedly(...)` are re-implemented here alongside `AbstractIntegrationTest`. The class comment explains convincingly why the two cannot share a superclass, but that argument does not extend to the helpers themselves — and `clickRepeatedly` has already drifted: it returns `List<Integer>` here and `List<HttpResponse<String>>` there, so the same name means two things depending on which base class a test extends.

findings.suggestion: Update §7 to match the delivered contract (or mark it superseded by artifacts/design.json), and change the `CacheConfig` javadoc to point at something that exists — the negative-caching rationale is already written in `LinkResolver` and `CachedLink`.
findings.summary: §7 of the committed "plan of record" now contradicts the service that was built: it states 410-for-expired vs 404-for-unknown (the design deliberately chose 404 for both), "Caffeine only — no Redis in the build" (the change is Redis-backed throughout), a `/api/v1/links/{code}/stats` endpoint, `Idempotency-Key`, an outbox, and 7-character codes (shipped: 22). Relatedly, `CacheConfig.LINKS_CACHE` cites "the enumeration note in ADR-004", but no ADR documents exist in the repo and the only ADR-004 reference is this plan's 7-character code decision.

findings.suggestion: Either drop the ones with no caller, or add a single line to each saying it is contract surface retained for future callers, so a later reader does not have to grep the whole repo to find out.
findings.summary: A handful of members exist for tests that never call them: `UrlValidator.ownHost()` and its no-arg constructor, `ShortCodeGenerator.random()` and its `SecureRandom` constructor, `RateLimitDecision.remaining()`, `LinkEntity.getDomain()`/`getCustomerId()`. They were plausibly frozen into the contract before the tests were written, which is a real reason — but as shipped they are surface nobody exercises.

findings.suggestion: Replace `\'` with `'` in the three AbuseReportService javadoc lines, and add the `java.util.UUID` import in `SignInService`.
findings.summary: Javadoc contains escaped apostrophes (`competitor\'s`, `customer\'s` on lines 35 and 36) — a shell-escaping artifact that renders literally in the generated docs. Separately, `SignInService.java:46` writes `java.util.UUID.randomUUID()` fully qualified where every other file in the change imports `java.util.UUID`.

not_examined: service/pom.xml dependency choices and versions (supply-chain/build concern, and argued in artifacts/design.json)
the 21 behaviour test classes under src/test/java/.../behaviour — read only for harness usage patterns, not for assertion adequacy (test-adequacy lens)
src/main/resources/redis/*.lua and db/migration/*.sql reviewed only for existence and call sites, not line by line
orchestrator/ and runs/ pipeline machinery — outside the change under review
correctness, concurrency and performance characteristics of the two-tier click counter (other lenses)
summary: This is unusually clean, consistent code for a greenfield change of this size: one naming vocabulary, one error catalogue, business rules in the service layer with the controllers doing routing and rate-limit charging only, no swallowed exceptions that are not explicitly argued for (every `catch (RuntimeException)` here is a documented fail-open with a log line at a defensible level, and the fail-open decisions log loudly enough to diagnose from), and comments that overwhelmingly explain *why* rather than *what*. Nothing I found is close to a blocker. The findings that will cost someone real time are duplications that must stay in agreement and have no mechanism keeping them so: the max-URL-length rule in three places with the configured copy dead (CLEAN-1), the alias regex literal duplicated with a comment acknowledging it (CLEAN-2), the flush interval bypassing the typed config surface everything else uses (CLEAN-3), the redirect-eligibility rule in two classes (CLEAN-4), and already-drifted helpers across the two test base classes (CLEAN-5). CLEAN-6 is documentation the change left contradicting the code. The remaining nits are few on purpose; other minor things I saw and did not file — near-verbatim rationale paragraphs repeated between `RateLimiter` and `RedisTokenBucketRateLimiter`, and between `RateLimitDecision.ALLOWED` and its implementation, plus `ThreatCheckConfig` living in `threat` while the other three `@Configuration` classes live in `config` — are minor and internally consistent.
